description.en: Quality, rating, or technical descriptor: out of focus.
Quality, rating, or technical descriptor: chromatic aberration.
description.zh: chromatic aberration（质量、分级与技术标签）

wiki.body_clean:
An effect where the edges of an image have a colored, blurry halo or fringe. The RGB color channels appear noticeably offset from one another.

In photography, chromatic aberration is caused by a defect of the camera lens. The lens refracts light of different wavelengths (colors) slightly differently (technically speaking, the index of refraction of a lens material varies depending on the wavelength), causing the colors to become out of focus.

In digital art, chromatic aberration is used to simulate a photographic look or for artistic effect. In small amounts it can increase realism; in greater amounts it can create a sense of motion (similar to motion blur), convey a chaotic environment, or indicate anxiety, paranoia, or mental derangement. In excessive amounts it can induce eyestrain.

Examples
- - - - External links
- Wikipedia: Chromatic aberration
- Photography Life: What is Chromatic Aberration?

wiki.body_clean:
Two or more different pictures of the same character in an image. These can be the same character from different viewpoints, in different outfits, in different poses, or any combination.

This tag doesn't apply to zoom layers unless the zoom layer is different from the foreground image. It also doesn't apply to comics, as they generally always have multiple views. If the images form a clear sequence over time, it is probably a comic with borderless panels or a sequential image instead.

Images with multiple views should not be tagged solo, as solo is for a single view of a single character.

For multiple distinct versions of the same character, see dual persona, clone, or time paradox.

wiki.body_clean:
A completely colorless, black-and-white image. The image is composed exclusively of shades of black, white, and grey. It is very common for comics and doujinshi to be in greyscale.

The image may have small highlights of color (known as spot colors), but the image as a whole should be predominately greyscale.

Don't use color tags like black eyes or black hair when tagging greyscale images. The exception is color background tags, so tagging white background, grey background, or black background is fine.

Guidelines
- For completely colorless art, use greyscale.
- For a post consisting of a single color that isn't grey, use monochrome, not greyscale.
- For a mostly greyscale post with a small amount of color as a highlight, use greyscale and spot color.
- For a post using a mix of color and greyscale, use partially colored, not greyscale.
- For a colorless foreground and colorful background, use greyscale with colored background, not greyscale or partially colored.
- For a post that has solid black shadings, use greyscale and high contrast.
- For posts with a small variety of colors but more than two actual colors, use limited palette, not greyscale or monochrome.

Examples
- - Spot color

Not greyscale
- Monochrome
- Sepia
- Partially colored
- Limited palette
- Muted colors

wiki.body_clean:
An image with an empty or featureless background. Commonly, a background that is solid white, transparent, or another color.

An image with a simple background takes place in an empty void, with no identifiable setting or location. This is opposed to an image that takes place in an identifiable setting, such as indoors or outdoors, or at day or night.

As a rule of thumb, there is nothing to tag in the background. Another rule of thumb is that the subject could easily be placed on a different background.

Simple colors and patterns, such as gradient backgrounds, grid backgrounds, striped backgrounds, etc, may also be considered simple backgrounds.

wiki.body_clean:
A photographic effect where circular out-of-focus points of light appear in the background of the image.

Bokeh can represent known light sources in the background of an image, but can also occur in seemingly random places all over the image. The latter, known as orbs are from light reflected off of particles in the air which would otherwise not be visible.

Lens flare artifacts can look similar to bokeh, but are due to bright light being reflected inside the camera, and don't line up with the original light source (which may not even be visible in the image).

Examples

- Wikipedia: Bokeh

When a non-human entity, such as an inanimate object, animal, creature, vehicle, etc, is depicted as a human or humanoid.

description.en: Character count or scene participant descriptor: humanoid.
Character count or scene participant descriptor: android.

wiki.body_clean:
A robot that looks human, or very nearly human, with a fully human face.

They may appear male, female, or androgynous. Female androids, also known as gynoids, are the most common in anime. Androids often have small robotic appendages or markings to make it apparent they are not human. The most common of these are robot ears, robot joints, skin seams, mechanical wings, and attached cables.

The difference between a humanoid robot and an android is that an android looks mostly human, usually having something resembling skin (though it needn't be skin-colored) and a fully human face, while a humanoid robot is clearly non-human, with a non-human face.

This tag should not be used if the character looks completely human, with no visible robotic traits. Tag what you see, not what you know.

Not to be confused with cyborg, which is a person augmented with mechanical body parts.

Examples
- Aigis
- Dorothy Haze
- A2
- Yurizaki Mira
- KOS-MOS (Ver. 4)

External links
- Wikipedia: Android

wiki.body_clean:
When a character who doesn't normally have animal-like features (such as ears or a tail) is drawn with animal ears or a tail.

This can also include characters who are canonically animal-like, but are depicted with a different set of animal features (for example, a dog girl being drawn as a cat girl). Note, however, that this does not include characters who can become animal-like, such as Inu Sakuya or the Strike Witches.

When there are more animal-like features like a snout or full fur, use furrification instead.

Not to be used when a character is wearing fake animal ears or a fake tail.

The opposite of this tag is no animal ears.

A character with animal ears, real or fake. Also known as kemonomimi. Do not use this tag for pictures of actual animals.

There are two areas where animal ears are usually placed. On top of the head and on the sides of the head (where a human's ears would be). The first type is much easier to accessorize but anatomically incorrect. The inverse is true for the second type. The first type is most likely to have extra human ears. An anthropomorphic animal; a character based on an animal but with human traits. Body fur, feathers, or scales are common. Characters that have only tails or ears are not considered furry, use kemonomimi mode instead.

"Kemono" is the Japanese equivalent of the term "furry", with fans of such being called "kemona" or "kemoner". Just like with furries in the west, there are numerous subcategories and subcultures within.

Monster girls or ordinary human characters with animal ears do not qualify for the furry tag.

wiki.body_clean:
When the stomach is left partially exposed by clothing.

The midriff is the region of the body between the chest and the waist. Use this tag when the midriff is left bare by clothing too short to cover the stomach, e.g. a crop top and pants. The stomach shouldn't be exposed much more than navel-height, though it can be higher to accommodate high-waist clothing.

Don't use this tag as a replacement for the stomach tag, or when the stomach is fully exposed. This includes when the character is nude, topless, bottomless, wearing only a bikini or underwear, or when their bottomwear isn't visible. It may be used for underwear worn as outerwear, such as sports bras, camisoles, tank tops worn with panties, etc.

description.en: Belly button
Inward-facing navel
Protruding navel

wiki.body_clean:
A belly button (navel) that outwardly protrudes from the belly of the character/person.

The inverse being an "innie" navel (where it appears to be sunken in a small pit on the belly).

Most often seen on pregnant women as the growing womb pushes on and out the navel from the inside, especially during middle to late stages of pregnancy. Can also be seen on males and non-pregnant females as well, generally associated with either non-pregnancy related belly expansion/inflation, or just how the belly button had ended up since the belly button (navel) is formed from the child side remains of the umbilical cord after birth and the cutting of said cord.
wiki.body_raw:
A belly button ([[navel]]) that outwardly protrudes from the belly of the character/person.

The inverse being an "innie" navel (where it appears to be sunken in a small pit on the belly).

Most often seen on [[pregnant]] women as the growing womb pushes on and out the navel from the inside, especially during middle to late stages of pregnancy. Can also be seen on males and non-pregnant females as well, generally associated with either non-pregnancy related belly expansion/inflation, or just how the belly button had ended up since the belly button (navel) is formed from the child side remains of the umbilical cord after birth and the cutting of said cord.

wiki.body_clean:
A bright ring or circle of light typically hovering above or traditionally behind the head that either symbolizes purity or to denote that the character is an angel or saint. This tag applies to all kinds of halos which hover over one's head, not just those that are considered traditional - for such halos only, see traditional halo.

Not to be confused with the optical phenomenon caused by ice crystals in the atmosphere surrounding the sun or moon, forming a halo, or halo-like artifacts of light caused by bright light sources interacting with the camera lens. The latter is a lens flare.

wiki.body_raw:
A bright ring or circle of light typically hovering above or traditionally behind the head that either symbolizes purity or to denote that the character is an [[angel]] or [[icon (religion)|saint]]. This tag applies to all kinds of halos which hover over one's head, not just those that are considered traditional - for such halos only, see [[traditional halo]].

Not to be confused with the optical phenomenon caused by ice crystals in the atmosphere surrounding the sun or moon, forming a halo, or halo-like artifacts of light caused by bright light sources interacting with the camera lens. The latter is a [[lens flare]].

description.en: Hair color or style: white hair.

wiki.body_clean:
Hair that is colored white.

Due to the subjective nature of color judgment, lighting, and color grading, there can be confusion between white hair and other hair colors in the very light color range. This especially true in regards to blue hair, purple hair, and grey hair. A good idea is to compare the hair color to any other white objects in the picture. If the hair is the same color, it should be tagged white hair. If it is darker or differently-colored, use the appropriate non-white tag.

description.en: Hair color or style: grey hair.

wiki.body_clean:
Hair that is colored grey.

Due to the subjective nature of color judgment and other factors (such as differences in color displayed on monitors) there is potential overlap between this tag and the blue hair, aqua hair, and purple hair tags, generally in the lighter shades of those colors. Grey is also often used to shade white hair. It is a good idea to compare the hair in question to how other white things, namely white clothes, are shaded. If the shading on the hair resembles how white clothing is shaded, it is likely white, and not grey.

- Light grey

description.en: Hair color or style: short hair.

wiki.body_clean:
Hair less than shoulder-length, typically around neck-length or shorter.

Short hairstyles include the bob cut, the inverted bob, the bowl cut, the flattop, the undercut, and short hair with long locks.

If the hair is ear length or shorter, it's very short hair; if it's shoulder length, it's medium hair.

Examples
- Bob cut
- Bowl cut
- Short hair with long locks
- "Default" (short), short, medium, long hair.

Hair lengths
- bald / bald female (no hair whatsoever)
- very short hair (shorter than jaw/chin length)
- short hair (shorter than shoulder length)
- medium hair (shoulder length)
- long hair (longer than shoulder length, up to waist length)
- very long hair (longer than waist length, up to floor length)
- absurdly long hair (beyond floor length)

description.en: Straight bangs cut in an even line

wiki.body_clean:
A hairstyle where the bangs are cut in a sharp, straight line across the entire length of the forehead. Mutually exclusive with swept bangs and asymmetrical bangs.

Known in Japan as パッツン (pattsun).

When combined with long hair and blunt sidelocks, it becomes a type of hime cut. If the bangs are shaved or combed back at the temples, with the rest hanging loose at the forehead it may result in center-flap bangs.

wiki.body_clean:
A hairstyle that consists of two braided lengths of hair.

If the braids are in front of the ears, they're braided sidelocks. If they're beside or behind the ears, they're side braids.

If the braids are tied low, below ear-level, they're low twin braids. If they're tied all the way up against the back of the scalp, then they're french braided twintails.

See multiple braids for more than two braids.

Examples
- - Braided sidelocks
- Side braids
- Low twin braids
- French braided twintails

Related tags

- french braided twintails
- low twin braids
- side braids 
- single braid
- multiple braids
- tri braids
- quad braids

- front ponytail

- twintails

A hair style where the hair is tied into sections forming two ponytails. The Japanese term for this type of hair style is ツインテール (twin tail).

All of the hair must be tied into two pigtails for this tag to count. If any hair outside of the bangs/sidelocks falls normally, it is two side up instead.

Not to be confused with multiple tails which relates to beings with more than one tail of the animal variety.

Examples

- Short twintails
- left is twintails, right is two side up

- Hatsune Miku (of VOCALOID)
- The eponymous character of Black Rock Shooter
- Fate Testarossa (of Lyrical Nanoha, only when transformed)
- Nakano Azusa (of K-ON!)
- Quess Paraya (Char's Counterattack)

wiki.body_clean:
A hairstyle consisting of long straight hair, blunt bangs, and sidelocks with blunt ends.

All elements must be present to be considered a hime cut. The hair must be long and straight and the bangs and sidelocks must have blunt ends.

As the name suggests, the style is thought to have originated, or at least become common, in the Imperial court during the Heian period of Japanese history, when noble women would sometimes grow out their hair for their entire lives.

description.en: Hair color, length, texture, or hairstyle: pixie cut.

wiki.body_clean:
A women's hairstyle, cut very short (around cheek length or less) on the sides and back of the head, while slightly longer on top.

The amount of styling varies, but it is usually unstyled. The cut often includes swept bangs that are positioned close to the eyes, creating a flattering and accentuated facial profile. They are typically low-maintenance, require minimal styling, and are a practical option for those who lead active lifestyles.

The hairstyle is often commonly associated with tomboy characters.

Examples
- Unstyled pixie 
- Styled pixie + undercut
- Pixie + messy hair
- Pixie + curly hair
- Pixie + wavy hair

description.en: Hair color, length, texture, or hairstyle: mullet.

wiki.body_clean:
Business in the front, party in the back.

A men's haircut that has waxed and waned in popularity since the 1970s. However, it is most associated with the 1980s, and it is considered the stereotypical male hairstyle of that period. The hair is cut short at the front and sides, but left long at the back. It has at times been associated with the rock and country music genres, lesbian subculture, and professional athletes.

A mullet with a narrow lock of hair tied or braided in the back is known as a rattail.

description.en: Facial feature, eye detail, or expression: slit pupils.
description.zh: slit pupils（面部、眼睛、嘴部与表情）

wiki.body_clean:
Pupils that are "non-circular" that appear to be stretched vertically or horizontally.

These style of eyes are commonly seen with animals like small felines, foxes, goats, lizards, snakes, and cephalopods. It is a common feature of fantasy creatures such as dragons, vampires, demons and other monster characters, as well.

Tsurime eyes sometimes have large irises with a pupil appearing slit, but this isn't sufficient to be actual "slit pupils". This is also distinct from [[|_|]].

Facial feature, eye detail, or expression: looking back.

wiki.body_clean:
A character turning their head, body or eyes to look behind themselves.

The subject's gaze should be directed fully or almost fully backwards over the shoulder, anywhere from 135 to 180 degrees behind them relative to their front.

Oftentimes combined with from behind and looking at viewer, and also sideways glance if the character's body is partly facing away.

If the character has both of their eyes closed, use facing back instead.

description.en: Facial feature, eye detail, or expression: looking to the side.

wiki.body_clean:
When a character's gaze is directed to something off to their side. Most commonly are eyes looking 90 degrees across the shoulder, but may also include up to 45 degrees facing in either direction.

Looking to the side is relative to the character's front, not the viewer's perspective. If the eyes are directed more than 45 degrees backwards use looking back instead.

If the character looks to the side without moving their head, combine with sideways glance. Not to be confused with averting eyes, where someone deliberately diverts their gaze from the viewer/others out of embarrassment , anger, annoyance, etc.

Examples
- Sideways glance

If the character looks to the side without moving their head, combine with [[sideways glance]]. Not to be confused with [[averting eyes]], where someone deliberately diverts their gaze from the viewer/others out of [[embarrassed|embarrassment]] , [[angry|anger]], [[annoyed|annoyance]], etc.

Do not use this tag when the character's face is shadowed simply because of a light source - use shade instead.

description.en: Sleeveless shirt

wiki.body_clean:
A shirt that has a neck, but that doesn't have any straps or sleeves.

Shirts that have straps, such as camisoles, tank tops, and spaghetti strap tops, aren't considered sleeveless because they don't have a neck. Likewise, strapless tops such as tube tops and off-shoulder shirts aren't considered sleeveless either, because they also don't have a neck. A sleeveless shirt is like a regular shirt with a neck and shoulders, but with the sleeves removed.

A sleeveless shirt may have detached sleeves or elbow gloves, since those are separate from the shirt.

Examples
- - - A sleeveless shirt worn with detached sleeves
- A sleeveless shirt worn with elbow gloves
- A sleeveless shirt worn with a jacket

Incorrect examples
- Strapless shirt
- Off-shoulder shirt
- Tube top

wiki.body_clean:
A form-fitting strapless top consisting of a continuous band of fabric wrapping around the torso, with the neckline stopping just above the breasts.

The length can range from covering the entire torso to covering just the breasts. If the midriff is exposed it may also be a crop top, while if only the breasts are covered it may be a bandeau. A tube top made of bandages is a sarashi.

Traditionally, the only support they provided was due to the stretchiness of the fabric. Tube tops do not have any attached sleeves, meaning that they leave the shoulders/arms and upper chest area bare.

Tube tops are innately strapless, thus they should not be tagged sleeveless, and they should not be used for any clothing with straps, shoulders, or sleeves.

Examples
- - Exposed midriff makes it also a crop top
- Narrow length additionally makes it a bandeau
- A bikini worn underneath a tube top
- A tube top worn underneath suspenders

A shoulder-less shirt with a wide low-cut neckline that is designed to leave the shoulders bare, with the sleeves resting on the upper arms instead of on top of the shoulders. The sleeves must be attached to the shirt.

description.en: Clothing item, fit, or outfit detail: leotard.

wiki.body_clean:
A skin tight, one-piece bodysuit that covers the torso but leaves the legs free. They are usually sleeveless. They usually have a very simple design (often even just a single color), and are typically made of light fabrics to accommodate athletic activities. They are most often worn by acrobats, gymnasts, dancers, and circus performers.

They also influenced the one-piece swimsuit design, but swimsuits should not be tagged as leotards.

If the leotard does cover at least the upper legs, do not use this tag. Use bodysuit instead.

description.en: Clothing item, fit, or outfit detail: bodysuit.

wiki.body_clean:
A skin tight, one-piece garment that covers the whole body, or most of it. Examples include mecha pilot suits, wetsuits, bikesuits, and superhero costumes.

A bodysuit is a single piece of clothing. If it's two separate pieces of clothing, such as a leotard over a pair of pantyhose, then it's not a bodysuit.

A bodysuit usually covers the whole body, from neck to toe. Some bodysuits may only cover the upper arms or legs, but this is the exception, not the rule. If it doesn't cover the arms at all, it's a sleeveless bodysuit. If it doesn't cover the arms or legs at all, like a one-piece swimsuit, then it's a leotard instead.

A bodysuit is usually made of sturdy material and worn by itself. If it's made of sheer or thin material, like pantyhose, then it's a bodystocking instead. If it's worn beneath other clothing, then it's probably not a bodysuit (unless it's a bodysuit under clothes).

If the dress is knee-length or shorter and less fancy, consider cocktail dress instead. Evening gowns are formal wear, so in real life they tend not to be extremely revealing, although in fanart this is often ignored.

description.en: Strapless dress

wiki.body_clean:
A dress that has no shoulder straps, attached sleeves, halterneck or other shoulder- or collarbone-related attire holding up the upper portion of the dress, instead relying on the tightness of the dress (usually around the hip or waist area) to keep it in place. The shoulders and upper chest area should be bare, which also implies the lack of a strapped bra.

Strapless dresses must not cover the shoulders or arms in any way outside of separate articles of clothing or jewelry such as detached sleeves, gloves, or armlets.

Strapless dresses, sleeveless dresses, and off-shoulder dresses are mutually exclusive to each other.

Correct examples
- - A strapless dress worn with elbow gloves
- A strapless dress worn with detached sleeves
- A strapless dress that has a bra worn underneath
- A strapless dress worn over a shirt
- A strapless dress (black) worn over a sleeveless outfit (grey)

Incorrect examples
Do not tag off-shoulder dresses as "strapless dress".

description.en: Sleeveless dress

wiki.body_clean:
A dress with no (attached) sleeves.

Sleeveless dress can be used together with detached sleeves, since sleeveless dress only refers to the torso garment, and do not take detached sleeves into account.

Do not confuse this tag as a "catch-all" tag for all dresses that simply leave the shoulders bare.
- If the dress has a low and wide-cut neckline and has attached sleeves that sit on the arms instead of on the shoulders, it is an off-shoulder dress.
- If the dress has no attached sleeves and has no support of the shoulders (ie. halternecks, shoulder straps, etc.) to keep it in place, it is a strapless dress.

Sleeveless dresses, strapless dresses, and off-shoulder dresses are mutually exclusive to each other.

Correct examples
- - - Incorrect examples
Do not tag strapless dresses as "sleeveless dress".
wiki.body_raw:
A [[dress]] with [[sleeveless|no (attached) sleeves]].

Sleeveless dress can be used together with [[detached sleeves]], since sleeveless dress only refers to the torso garment, and do not take detached sleeves into account.

Do not confuse this tag as a "catch-all" tag for all dresses that simply leave the shoulders [[bare shoulders|bare]].
* If the dress has a [i]low and wide-cut neckline[/i] and has [i]attached[/i] sleeves that sit on the arms instead of on the shoulders, it is an [[off-shoulder dress]].

description.en: Tight cycling shorts

wiki.body_clean:
Tight, form-fitting athletic shorts composed of nylon and Spandex that reach about mid-thigh.

The primary purposes of bike shorts are to compress muscles (particularly the groin and thighs), prevent chafing, help remove sweat, keep muscles warm, and keep male genitals in place. There are two similar appearing types of these, compression shorts and bike shorts. Both types may be used without underwear, depending on if they were designed to act as underwear.

On Danbooru, the most common version depicted are compression shorts, which are used for a variety of sports and athletic activities. Compression shorts are similar to bike shorts, but aren't designed with biking in mind and thus lack things like padding to reduce discomfort from long rides. Compression shorts are sometimes used by some women to conceal their panties beneath their skirt, especially for those in women's sports where their uniform has a skirt, such as field hockey or lacrosse.

In Japan, these are also known as spats, and this meaning has spread across otaku spaces. They are considered a type of short leggings there. For the Jazz Age footwear, see spats.

description.en: Lower-body garment, legwear, or footwear: bloomers.

wiki.body_clean:
A type of underwear constructed much like boxer shorts worn by women. Most bloomers, unlike boxers, are gathered at the bottom of the legs. Often bloomers will be decorated with ribbon or frills at the waist and legs. In Japanese they are sometimes translated as kabopan or "pumpkin pants".

Not to be confused with buruma, an English to Japanese to English translation of bloomer, usually identifying an over-panty, or a public garment whose purpose is to cover the panty and crotch area while leaving the maximum maneuvering room.

While bloomers originally served as underwear, they are not necessarily considered underwear now. Traditional bloomers can go all the way to the knees or shins, and don't resemble typical underwear in the present day. Shorter bloomers can be worn as regular shorts or safety shorts. These shouldn't be tagged as underwear nor pantyshot. Note that this doesn't mean they can't be sensitive, rating:S and tags like upskirt still apply.

Examples
- As safety shorts
- As underwear
- As shorts
- Long bloomers

description.en: Lower-body garment, legwear, or footwear: tabi.

wiki.body_clean:
A kind of traditional Japanese sock. Modern tabi resemble regular socks, only there is a division between the big toe and the other toes in order to be worn with thonged footwear. Historically, Tabi are commonly made of inelastic materials such as leather and cotton and have fasteners at the back due to its origin as indoor footwear, but modern Tabi also use stretchable fabrics.

For socks with division between all toes use toe socks instead.

For tabi that are used as footwear, use jika-tabi instead.

Examples
- - You can't wear sandals with regular socks

description.en: Strapless bra

wiki.body_clean:
A bra without straps, relying on an extra-wide band for breast support.

They are designed to be worn with strapless clothing that would otherwise expose the bra straps. They achieve their strength through a longer underwire that encompasses more of the breast, and cups with added padding, boning, and shaping panels. Some have rubberized or silicone beading inside the top edge of the cup to help keep the bra attached to the breast. Some convertible bras allow the straps to be removed, making them into strapless bras.

Don't confuse strapless bras with tube tops or bandeaus. A strapless bra has cups, while tube tops and bandeaus don't.

description.en: Underwear, swimwear, or revealing garment: chemise.

wiki.body_clean:
A loose-fitting top with thin spaghetti straps, usually ending past the waist, typically worn as sleepwear or lingerie.

A chemise typically does not have any buttons or other fasteners and is put on by either dropping it over the head or stepping into it and lifting it up. Its usually on the plainer side, being worn under clothes to smoothe the silhouette.

A chemise is similar to a babydoll, which is also a short, loose-fitting, sleeveless garment. Typically, though, babydolls have a front slit, may flare at the hips, and may have an empire waist, which chemises do not.

wiki.body_clean:
A bikini is a two-piece swimsuit for women, typically comprising a bra-like top and a panty-like bottom; however, the bottom can also be in the style of a bikini skirt or bikini shorts.

Bikinis come in a wide range of styles, with most designed to reveal more of the body, especially around the midriff and cleavage.

The key distinguishing feature of a bikini is that it prominently exposes the midriff, whereas other types of two-piece swimsuits may have a higher waistline and/or a top that extends further to cover the area. However, it's worth noting that most modern two-piece swimsuits are, in fact, bikinis.

If only the bra portion of the bikini is worn, use bikini top only. Likewise, use bikini bottom only when only the panty portion is worn. If a character's bikini top and bottom don't match, use mismatched bikini.

description.en: Competition-style athletic swimsuit

wiki.body_clean:
A type of performance-optimized one-piece swimsuit that is commonly worn in swimming meets and competitions. They are different from more casual one-pieces in having a racerback as opposed to "backless" ones, and they appear to have a slimming effect, allowing for easier movement through the water. Real-world designs also tend not to emphasize cleavage, since having the chest area exposed is not optimal for hydrodynamics.

There are also unisexual competition swimsuits that resemble bodysuits and wetsuits and cover either the legs or the thighs (like bike shorts). These unisex suits have become standard wear in international swimming competitions for both sexes (especially for women) in recent decades as a modesty measure, something yet to be applied in diving and synchronized swimming events.

Some of the following companies' logos are apparent in such swimsuits:

- Adidas
- Arena
- Asics
- Mizuno
- Speedo

description.en: Underwear, swimwear, or revealing garment: school swimsuit.

wiki.body_clean:
A standard school-issued one-piece swimsuit usually blue, black, white or grey in color sometimes with the wearer's name written or printed on a white name tag stitched across the chest. The style has evolved over the years.

The original old school swimsuit has thicker shoulder straps, vertical seams over torso and a flap over the groin. The new school swimsuit is the same, except with no flap over the groin.

The competition school swimsuit has thinner shoulder straps, is unseamed and has no flap over the groin. It is closer in style to the more modern competition swimsuit, but still in the style of a school swimsuit.

The non-traditional school swimsuit is a swimsuit that has been patterned after a school swimsuit, but is two-piece, frilled, or has other alterations to it that deviate from the norm.

Examples
- - Old school swimsuit  (Thick straps, flap)
- New school swimsuit  (Thick straps, no flap)
- Competition school swimsuit  (Thin straps, no flap)

description.en: Headwear, jewelry, or accessory: headband.

A bow that is tied around the neck. Often seen on female school uniforms, where they have loose ends.

A traditional bowtie doesn't have loose ends and is commonly seen in formal male clothing such as a tuxedo, and in playboy bunny outfits (usually attached to a detached collar).

Not to be confused with a neck ribbon which lacks the volume of the bowtie.

- Bowtie with loose ends
- Bowties resemble a butterfly or two triangles

- Ribbon choker. Wraps tightly around the neck and has direct contact with the skin
- Bow choker
- Neckerchief. A piece of cloth resembling a necktie, there is no bow.

description.en: Surgical mask

wiki.body_clean:
A mouth mask of the type worn by doctors and nurses to prevent the spread of bacteria from the wearer's mouth and nose.  It is composed of a rectangular piece of cloth with several horizontal folds to allow it to stretch over the mouth and nose.

This term refers to two similar types of medical masks, a procedure mask and surgical mask. Procedure masks may not be sterile and fasten by looping around the ears; used when carrying out general medical procedures like a check-up. Surgical masks are sterile and are fastened by bands that loop around the head; used when carrying out surgeries.

In Japan, it is common to wear a face mask whilst ill to avoid infecting others in public settings. During the coronavirus pandemic, it became common to wear masks worldwide.

They are also worn by delinquents, from school renegades to bousouzoku and the yakuza.

Examples
- External links
- Wikipedia: Surgical mask

description.en: Gas mask

wiki.body_clean:
A full-face mask that protects the wearer from toxic gases and airborne pollutants by covering their nose, mouth, and eyes.

They protect the wearer by forming a sealed cover over the nose and mouth and filters the air that they breath in to prevent inhaling toxic gases or pollutants. The mask also protects the eyes from exposure to toxic gases or pollutants that may cause irritation, temporary blindness, or even permanent eye damage.

If the mask doesn't cover the eyes, then it's a respirator, not a gas mask.

description.en: Headwear, jewelry, or accessory: wand.

wiki.body_clean:
A short, thin, hand-held stick made of wood, stone, ivory, or metal, with ceremonial or magical significance.

It is generally used as a magical tool to cast or channel magic just like a mage staff. Differences between a stave and a wand include a staff being larger (several feet long, about the length of a walking stick and held one- or two-handed) than a wand (usually shorter than two feet, held in one hand or a few fingers) and that a wand is often used in less "serious" works especially by fairies or fairy godmothers and can imply a playful form of magic.

Laevatein, associated with Flandre Scarlet, is an example of a more unusual wand.

Not to be confused with conductor baton, sometimes also referred to as a wand.

Common accessories can include: sweater, cardigan, sweater vest, thighhighs, and kneehighs. A gakuran is a popular uniform worn by boys. A common footwear for both genders while in school is the uwabaki.

Many types of school uniforms exist. See list of uniforms for a full list.

description.en: Uniform, profession, or themed costume: serafuku.

wiki.body_clean:
The school uniform with a sailor-style collar worn by Japanese schoolgirls in middle school and high school. The standard uniform consists of a white blouse, a pleated skirt, and a red neckerchief, but there are as many variations as there are stars in the sky.

Serafukus are commonly worn with a ribbon or bow in lieu of the traditional neckerchief. The line between "neckerchief" and "bow" is blurry, as the bows worn with serafukus often aren't actually dedicated bows or bowties, but rather a neckerchief tied into a bow instead of its intended scarf-like shape.

A serafuku always includes a skirt. If a sailor-style top is paired with shorts or another bottom, sailor shirt should be used instead. In fact, sailor suits with shorts are the older, original style: in the Victorian and Edwardian eras, they were used as boys' suits, from which then the girls' uniform with a skirt was derived.

For colored serafuku tags, both the shirt and skirt must match in color to apply, but not the neckwear or sailor collar.

Sailor dresses should not be tagged as serafuku.

description.en: Uniform, profession, or themed costume: school swimsuit.

wiki.body_clean:
A standard school-issued one-piece swimsuit usually blue, black, white or grey in color sometimes with the wearer's name written or printed on a white name tag stitched across the chest. The style has evolved over the years.

The original old school swimsuit has thicker shoulder straps, vertical seams over torso and a flap over the groin. The new school swimsuit is the same, except with no flap over the groin.

The competition school swimsuit has thinner shoulder straps, is unseamed and has no flap over the groin. It is closer in style to the more modern competition swimsuit, but still in the style of a school swimsuit.

The non-traditional school swimsuit is a swimsuit that has been patterned after a school swimsuit, but is two-piece, frilled, or has other alterations to it that deviate from the norm.

Examples
- - Old school swimsuit  (Thick straps, flap)
- New school swimsuit  (Thick straps, no flap)
- Competition school swimsuit  (Thin straps, no flap)

wiki.body_clean:
A person who wears a western (specifically Anglo-French)-style or influenced maid uniform.

In anime, maids typically wear some variation of the classic French or English maid uniform (the former is primarily decorative, with frills, short skirt, and bib apron, while the latter is usually an ankle-length or mid-calf length dark-colored dress with a pinafore apron). The most indicative sign that a woman is a maid is a white maid headdress and some sort of white maid apron.

If a character that is not usually portrayed with a maid uniform is drawn with one, also add the enmaided tag.

See wa maid for traditional Japanese maids, or qi maid for Chinese maids.

A professional who cooks food in a restaurant for a living. There are different ranks of chefs, such as the executive chef as the boss who runs the kitchen and designs the menu, the sous chef who assists the executive, and the chef de partie, otherwise known as the line cook.

Their uniform consists of a white or black double-breasted jacket, a chef hat for higher-ranking chefs and a pillbox hat for lower-ranking cooks, an apron, black slacks, and heavy shoes.

description.zh: playboy bunny（制服、职业与主题服装）

wiki.body_clean:
A woman wearing the uniform of a Playboy bunny (sometimes referred to unofficially as a "bunnysuit"). In Japan, the concept has been divorced from the Playboy brand, and they are simply known as "bunny girls".

The Playboy bunny uniform typically consists of a black strapless leotard (technically a corset), fake rabbit ears (usually in the form of a hairband), a fake rabbit tail, detached wrist cuffs, a white detached collar with a black bowtie, black or brown pantyhose, and black high heels. Common variations include substituting the pantyhose with fishnets or thighhighs, and the omission of any part of the outfit other than the ears and leotard.

A Playboy Bunny was originally a cocktail waitress who worked at a Playboy Club. The first Playboy Bunny costume was introduced when Hugh Hefner opened his first Playboy Club in Chicago in 1960.

description.en: Uniform, profession, or themed costume: miko.

wiki.body_clean:
A shrine maiden in a Shinto shrine.

They sweep the shrine, do ceremonial dances, perform music, flank the priest at prayers, freshen the offerings, operate the fortune telling lottery (omikuji), sell votive tablets (ema), and in most modern shrines run the knickknack and good luck charms shop. Historically, they used to be mediums and oracles, alongside the male Geki. They often carry gohei, wooden wands with paper streamers called shide.

Their traditional outfit consists of a white kosode top and a red hakama skirt. Miko who do not wear the traditional outfit should be tagged as nontraditional miko instead. Hakurei Reimu and Yae Miko are prominent examples of this.

description.en: Traditional Japanese pleated hakama trousers

wiki.body_clean:
Traditional Japanese clothing, looking like either a pleated skirt (a hakama skirt) or baggy, pleated pants (hakama pants). A traditional hakama has seven deep pleats, five in the front and two in the rear.

Hakama are split into a front and back section at the top, which are tied at the waist, often with visible hip vents and usually covering the midriff. Hakama are normally worn over a kimono and are very often red in color, although any color may be used. Traditional hakama are long garments, but non-traditional hakama short skirts and hakama shorts are often seen in anime.

Hakama were commonly worn both by samurai, miko and kannushi, practitioners of many martial arts including kyuudou, and often by sumo wrestlers when appearing in public outside the ring.

They were traditionally worn by men with either a kataginu sleeveless jacket/vest in an outfit known as kamishimo (lit. upper & lower) or over a formal, long-sleeved montsuki kimono, with the family crest on it. Sometimes a haori is worn over the latter.

During the late 19th and early 20th centuries, they were part of the standard female Meiji schoolgirl uniform until the introduction of the serafuku. They were commonly worn by both female college students and female teachers or professors at graduation ceremonies. They were also a fashionable day to day outfit for young women during this time period, often paired with a kimono with a simple geometric or floral print. Women's hakama tend to be either solid color or with a graduated hue, and hakama meant for young women may be sparsely decorated with floral decorations, paired with a solid color kimono.

Examples
- Hakama pants
- Hakama shorts
- Meiji schoolgirl uniform with long hakama skirt
- Hakama short skirt

description.en: Uniform, profession, or themed costume: kimono.

wiki.body_clean:
A type of traditional Japanese clothing, consisting of a long, wide-sleeved robe, closed at the front forming a "y" shape. It is held closed with a wide belt-like sash called an obi. The sleeves can be tied back with tasuki.

Kimonos are often worn with other traditional accessories, such as zouri (traditional wooden sandals), tabi (split-toe socks), and kanzashi (traditional hair ornaments). A kinchaku (small cloth drawstring bag) is often carried while wearing a kimono.

Kimonos come in many different styles for different occasions. Yukata are worn during summer to summer festivals or to onsens. Furisode are formal kimonos worn by unmarried women. Uchikake and shiromuku are worn by brides during wedding ceremonies.

Juban are usually worn under the kimono as the inner layer, and used by some as sleepwear.

description.en: Traditional Japanese haori jacket

wiki.body_clean:
A wide-sleeved silk jacket worn over a kimono. Mostly worn by men, this jacket is at hip- or thigh-length. There may be a decorative tie string called haori himo across the chest or the middle of the jacket.

Shinsengumi are identified by a light blue haori, with sleeves trimmed with white dandara-moyou (mountain stripes).

Not to be confused with kataginu, which more resembles a vest than a traditional jacket, or with happi, which has tube-sleeves, instead of kimono sleeves.

wiki.body_clean:
Historical styles of clothing worn by the Han Chinese. Most styles have a “y” shape collar, but there are also styles with a rounded collar.

There are several styles that are at times mistaken for kimono (most notably ruqun). You can typically distinguish between them based on the hairstyle and headwear. Males' hair may be pulled back into a simple ponytail or bun or held by a coronet. Emperors or princes may wear mian guan. If nothing else, huadian (forehead mark), or the circular fan is an easy distinguishing mark.

Hanfu differs from Qing era clothing. Hanfu specifically refers to clothing worn during dynasties wherein the ruling class was made up of the majority Chinese ethnic group, the Han. The Qing Dynasty was ruled by the Manchu ethnic minority. The frog button and mandarin collar style clothes, often simply referred to as Chinese clothes, are not Hanfu, as they are not Han clothing, but in fact Manchu. This goes too for other ethnic minority clothing in China, such as Miao clothes or Uygur clothes. These fall under the umbrella of Chinese clothes, along with hanfu.

wiki.body_clean: The ao dai (Vietnamese: áo dài) is a Vietnamese national costume, now most commonly for women. It is a two-part outfit consisting of a long tunic (often looking similar to a dress) and trousers. The top is usually tightly fitted with a high or mandarin collar and is often made of bright colors and decorated with floral patterns. The trousers are typically made of silk, with a contrasting color to the top.

Gothic Lolita (ゴスロリ, "GothLoli", or sometimes "Loli-Goth") is a specific kind of fashion that is a mixture of both goth and Lolita fashion. Lolita fashion draws much of its inspiration from Rococo, Victorian-style and Edwardian fashion and often aims to imitate the look of Victorian children or porcelain dolls. Gothic Lolita applies the aesthetics of goth fashion to the childlike, pretty Lolita fashion.

wiki.body_clean:
Sweet Lolita or "Amaloli" ( アマーロリ ) is a substyle of Lolita fashion heavily influenced by Rococo styles as well as Victorian and Edwardian children's clothing. Focusing on the child and fantasy aspects of Lolita, the Sweet Lolita style adopts the basic Lolita format and uses lighter colors.

It has all the traditional Lolita elements but with a wider choice of colors, like light pinks, baby blues, whites, and even sometimes colors like lavender, canary yellow and mint green. This is also where you'll find the most fluff and frills.

A style of Lolita fashion heavily based on historical fashion. It tends to have a "mature/elegant" Victorian look to it.

Skirts in Classic Lolita are usually longer than in Sweet Lolita, and feature motifs such as floral print, crowns, realistic animals, and fine art. Overall, the style tends to have a more sophisticated appearance. Dresses and skirts may have a more "A-line" silhouette as opposed to the more poofy one.

A Japanese fashion style influenced by Victorian children's clothing as well as costumes from the Rococo movement.

The fashion consists primarily of a knee length skirt or dress, headdress, blouse, petticoat/crinoline, knee length socks or stockings and rocking horse shoes, high heels or mary janes. Teddy bears and dolls are often carried to emphasize the childlike look.

Posts under this tag do not necessarily have to follow all of the real life modesty rules of Lolita (such as covering the shoulders), but should match the general aesthetic and silhouette. Not everything with frills is necessarily Lolita. Traditional depictions of Lolita coordinates can be found in the tag accurate Lolita coord.

Please note that Lolita fashion and loli are two very different things. Older women can be shown wearing these clothes as well.

wiki.body_clean:
Japanese fashion style that peaked in the 2000s. Although it has generally declined in real life, it remains popular in anime and fanart.

It has many diverse substyles, but typically involves tanned skin, styled and colored hair (sometimes bleached blonde), trendy and often sexy clothing (especially from the shops in the mall Shibuya 109), and heavy gyaru makeup, with a focus on false eyelashes, enlarging the eyes, contouring, and circle lenses. Additionally, many gyaru use the "gyaru-moji" (ギャル文字) style of typing and certain specialized slang (ギャル語). There are also certain common hobbies among gyaru: dancing Para Para was at one time a very popular activity in gyaru circles.

Two common elements of gyaru looks, especially in anime and manga representations, are tanned skin (ganguro - especially for older or throwback styles) and bleached hair. However, not every gyaru has tanned skin or bleached hair, and not every character with tanned skin and bleached hair is a gyaru.

Gyaru are usually depicted as energetic or extroverted. In adult media they may be depicted either as a high-school student prostitute or as having an unusually high sex drive.

Male gyarus are known as gyaruo. Do not add the gyaruo tag to a trap who dresses up as a gyaru.

wiki.body_clean:
Kogal (コギャル), a substyle of Gyaru (ギャル), is a fashion trend among young female Japanese high school students.

They follow the trends of gyaru fashion in their heavy makeup (especially around the eyes), sometimes tan skin, use of English-influenced slang (kogyarugo or コギャル語), coloured (and often bleached) hair, and trendy gyaru style fashion. Since they are school girls, they use their school uniform as their fashion statement, often wearing their uniform skirts very short and paired with loose socks.

If there aren't any obvious signs of kogal (school uniform, loose socks, scrunchie, etc) then it's recommended to just tag the image with the more general gyaru.

A science fiction genre. Basic themes include the dehumanizing effects of technology, and the accompanying societal breakdown. Think dark and dirty, with lots of wires and neon.

Cyberpunk is a postmodern dystopian genre noted for its focus on ”high tech and low life". The name is a portmanteau of cybernetics and punk, and was originally coined by American science fiction author Bruce Bethke as the title of his short Sci-Fi story Cyberpunk, written in 1980 (and further popularized by the famous American sci-fi author William Gibson).

Cyberpunk can cover numerous themes and motifs but generally involve reflecting on the current anxieties of society and amping them up to an extreme; things like mass surveillance, corporate monopolization, climate change, mass media, artificial intelligence and any other themes can thus be accommodated by a cyberpunk setting.

For the series of the same name, see Cyberpunk.

description.en: Chainmail armor made of interlinked rings

wiki.body_clean:
Armor made from small metal rings linked together into a mesh. Also known as simply "mail" or "maille."

European garments made with mail are leggings (chausses), mail hoods (coif) and mail mittens (mitons). A mail collar hanging from a helmet is camail or aventail. A mail collar worn strapped around the neck was called a pixane or standard. A shirt made from mail is a hauberk if knee-length and a haubergeon if mid-thigh length.

Japanese chainmail is called kusari (鎖, lit. "chain") and was used extensively alongside the more distinctive and better known lamellar armors.

Examples

- Shields

description.en: Priestess in ceremonial attire
Nun

wiki.body_clean:
A lay woman who has taken special vows committing her to a religious life, otherwise known as a religious sister. They must adopt a celibate life, refraining from marriage and sexual relationships - a religious sister takes part in a religious institution, while a nun lives a cloistered monastic life. They are recognized by their distinctive set of garments, called a habit. Christian ones can be additionally recognized by the appearance of a cross or crucifix.

The term "nun" is applicable to Catholics – both Eastern and Western traditions – Orthodox Christians, Anglicans, Lutherans, Jains, Buddhists, and Taoists. Nuns can vary in appearance not just across each tradition, but within traditions as well; common subtypes of nuns across traditions include military nuns (or battle/combat/warrior nuns).

See traditional nun for the traditional modest Christian nun outfit, as opposed to the sexualized nun outfits typically seen in anime. See nun headdress for the collective clothing that makes up a nun's headdress.

Examples

- military nun

Clothing

- guimpe
- wimple/coif

A being in folklore who feeds on the blood of living creatures. Notable characteristics include fangs, predatory eyes, pale skin and a bite mark on the neck.

Although typically described as undead, a vampire could be a living person. Popularized in Europe in the 18th century and codified in literature in the 19th century as a Western folkloric being distinct from its Slavic(-Turkic) roots.

Common beliefs about vampires include that they are immortal, that they can only be killed by being exposed to the sun or by a wooden stake driven through their heart, that they sleep in coffins, have no reflections, are afraid of crosses and garlic, are able to hypnotize victims, are able to transform into bats, and that they are unable to enter homes without being invited in. Half-vampires are often called 'dhampir' in English, which means vampire in Albanian.

This tag should not be used unless vampiric traits are clearly visible in the image. See vampire costume for when a character is simply dressed as a vampire.

For the game produced by Capcom, see Darkstalkers.

Bride in wedding attire

wiki.body_clean:
A woman getting married in a wedding ceremony.

Bridalwear differs across cultures. Usually a bride in a western wedding wears a long white wedding dress, a bridal veil, and carries a bouquet of flowers. A Japanese bride wears a shiromuku (a white kimono with red trim), a wataboushi (a white hood), and may carry accessories tucked into their kimono, such as a folding fan, a hakoseko (a wallet), and a futokorogatana ("chest sword", a small dagger held in a purse).

wiki.body_clean:
Wariza (割座), also known as "w-sitting" or "reverse tailor style sitting" in English, is a sitting posture whereby the butt is on the floor and the legs are bent backwards on each side of the body. It is the traditional informal sitting style for Japanese women. If the legs are folded out to only one side, then it is called yokozuwari.

The other Japanese names are: 女の子座り (onna-no-ko-zuwari, girl's sitting), アヒル座り (ahiru-zuwari, duck sitting) or ぺたん座り (petan-zuwari, flat surface sitting). (In fact, in Japanese, wariza more commonly refers to a yoga pose.)

description.en: Saluting gesture

wiki.body_clean:
A gesture of greeting and respect, typically a hand raised in the air.

Salutes vary across countries and even within different branches of the military in the same country. American salutes consist of the forearm at a 45° angle to the forehead, with the blade hand with palm towards face. British salutes are similar, but with the palm facing outward. The straight-arm salute (also called the Roman or Nazi salute) has the arm extended straight out and upwards.

A salute should not be confused with simple waving or making the V sign.

Examples
- American salute
- British salute
- Zogist salute
- Two-finger salute
- Straight-arm salute
- Vulcan salute

Related tags
- Two-finger salute 
- Three-finger salute
- Straight-arm salute 
- Super Earth Salute (Helldivers)
- Vulcan salute

External links
- Wikipedia: Salute

description.en: Camera framing, point of view, or composition: foreshortening.

wiki.body_clean:
A technique in which an object is depicted at an angle, making it appear shorter than its actual size. This captures the distortion seen when viewing an object at an unusual angle.

Not to be confused with depth of field, which refers to blurry, out-of-focus portions of an image. An image can contain both, but not necessarily.

Poorly done foreshortening may result in bad perspective.

wiki.body_clean:
A photographic effect where circular out-of-focus points of light appear in the background of the image.

Bokeh can represent known light sources in the background of an image, but can also occur in seemingly random places all over the image. The latter, known as orbs are from light reflected off of particles in the air which would otherwise not be visible.

Lens flare artifacts can look similar to bokeh, but are due to bright light being reflected inside the camera, and don't line up with the original light source (which may not even be visible in the image).

Examples

- Wikipedia: Bokeh

description.en: Camera framing, point of view, or composition: lens flare.
description.zh: lens flare（构图、镜头与画面裁切）

wiki.body_clean:
An optical artifact caused by light entering a lens from an unwanted direction. The image-forming capability of optical systems rely on most light traveling a known, coherent path through it from a particular direction, usually straight ahead. Light from other directions of sufficient intensity can reflect and scatter in pathways other than the intended one, which appears as bright patches of various shapes and sizes in the image.

Lens flare generally appears in three different ways. Each can appear by itself or with another in any combination, although pictures with the third type are more likely to use it exclusively:
- Bright streaks radiating from the light source. 
- Circles or polygons of various pale colors and sizes centered on a line pointing to the light source. These shapes are multiple images of the camera's diaphragm aperture, also known as an iris. Cameras with 5-bladed irises will produce pentagons, 6-bladed hexagons, etc., with more blades producing a progressively more circular shape. These can appear even if the light source is outside the field of view.
- Anamorphic lenses are a special type of lens that have been used extensively in movie cameras since the 1950's. They produce a characteristic lens flare similar to the first, except streaks are strictly horizontal. Streaks in other directions are either not present or much fainter. Because of its use in the film industry, for most people this type of lens flare has a very strong association with movies, and this effect is often simulated to impart a cinematic quality.

If it goes too far, you get heavy lens flare.

Examples
- Type 1 (streaks, with prominent halos (see below))
- Type 1+2 (streaks and hexagons)
- Type 1+2 (streaks and circles)
- Type 3 (anamorphic type)

The following are NOT lens flares:
- Rainbow-colored arcs that partially or entirely encircle the light source. These are most likely halos Halos are not camera artifacts; like rainbows, they are caused by light being reflected and refracted by water droplets or ice crystals in the atmosphere.
- bokeh. Bokeh is affected by the shape and size of a camera's iris in the same way as the second type of lens flare. However bokeh does not appear in a line, instead each spot corresponds to a single, out-of-focus light source.
- "Love bubbles": In anime, manga and associated illustrations, to give a scene a "lovey-dovey" or "dreamy" feeling, often the artist draws many translucent circles in the background and around the edges of the image. While sometimes appearing similar to lens flare, they have no corresponding light source. These can even appear in dark pictures with no bright light sources at all.

External Links
- Wikipedia: Lens Flare

description.en: Camera framing, point of view, or composition: chromatic aberration.
description.zh: chromatic aberration（构图、镜头与画面裁切）

wiki.body_clean:
An effect where the edges of an image have a colored, blurry halo or fringe. The RGB color channels appear noticeably offset from one another.

In photography, chromatic aberration is caused by a defect of the camera lens. The lens refracts light of different wavelengths (colors) slightly differently (technically speaking, the index of refraction of a lens material varies depending on the wavelength), causing the colors to become out of focus.

In digital art, chromatic aberration is used to simulate a photographic look or for artistic effect. In small amounts it can increase realism; in greater amounts it can create a sense of motion (similar to motion blur), convey a chaotic environment, or indicate anxiety, paranoia, or mental derangement. In excessive amounts it can induce eyestrain.

Examples
- - - - External links
- Wikipedia: Chromatic aberration
- Photography Life: What is Chromatic Aberration?

This tag doesn't apply to zoom layers unless the zoom layer is different from the foreground image. It also doesn't apply to comics, as they generally always have multiple views. If the images form a clear sequence over time, it is probably a comic with borderless panels or a sequential image instead.

Images with multiple views should not be tagged solo, as solo is for a single view of a single character.

For multiple distinct versions of the same character, see dual persona, clone, or time paradox.

wiki.body_clean:
A character, often full body, shown from multiple views about their vertical axis while usually keeping the same pose and outfit. A technique commonly used on reference sheets to demonstrate a character's entire design. This varies from a simple straight-on (0º) and facing away (180º) view, to supplemental in-between angles such as the side (90º) and 45º views.

For characters literally turning their head or body around, use turning around instead.

description.zh: lens flare（光照、色彩、氛围与特效）

wiki.body_clean:
An optical artifact caused by light entering a lens from an unwanted direction. The image-forming capability of optical systems rely on most light traveling a known, coherent path through it from a particular direction, usually straight ahead. Light from other directions of sufficient intensity can reflect and scatter in pathways other than the intended one, which appears as bright patches of various shapes and sizes in the image.

Lens flare generally appears in three different ways. Each can appear by itself or with another in any combination, although pictures with the third type are more likely to use it exclusively:
- Bright streaks radiating from the light source. 
- Circles or polygons of various pale colors and sizes centered on a line pointing to the light source. These shapes are multiple images of the camera's diaphragm aperture, also known as an iris. Cameras with 5-bladed irises will produce pentagons, 6-bladed hexagons, etc., with more blades producing a progressively more circular shape. These can appear even if the light source is outside the field of view.
- Anamorphic lenses are a special type of lens that have been used extensively in movie cameras since the 1950's. They produce a characteristic lens flare similar to the first, except streaks are strictly horizontal. Streaks in other directions are either not present or much fainter. Because of its use in the film industry, for most people this type of lens flare has a very strong association with movies, and this effect is often simulated to impart a cinematic quality.

If it goes too far, you get heavy lens flare.

Examples
- Type 1 (streaks, with prominent halos (see below))
- Type 1+2 (streaks and hexagons)
- Type 1+2 (streaks and circles)
- Type 3 (anamorphic type)

The following are NOT lens flares:
- Rainbow-colored arcs that partially or entirely encircle the light source. These are most likely halos Halos are not camera artifacts; like rainbows, they are caused by light being reflected and refracted by water droplets or ice crystals in the atmosphere.
- bokeh. Bokeh is affected by the shape and size of a camera's iris in the same way as the second type of lens flare. However bokeh does not appear in a line, instead each spot corresponds to a single, out-of-focus light source.
- "Love bubbles": In anime, manga and associated illustrations, to give a scene a "lovey-dovey" or "dreamy" feeling, often the artist draws many translucent circles in the background and around the edges of the image. While sometimes appearing similar to lens flare, they have no corresponding light source. These can even appear in dark pictures with no bright light sources at all.

External Links
- Wikipedia: Lens Flare

If it goes too far, you get [[heavy lens flare]].

h4. Examples

* !post #5341001: Type 1 (streaks, with prominent halos (see below))
* !post #716920: Type 1+2 (streaks and hexagons)
* !post #10228790: Type 1+2 (streaks and circles)
* !post #2298239: Type 3 (anamorphic type)

The following are NOT lens flares:
* Rainbow-colored arcs that partially or entirely encircle the light source. These are most likely "halos":https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halo_(optical_phenomenon). Halos are not camera artifacts; like [[rainbow]]s, they are caused by light being reflected and refracted by water droplets or ice crystals in the atmosphere.
* [[bokeh]]. Bokeh is affected by the shape and size of a camera's iris in the same way as the second type of lens flare. However bokeh does not appear in a line, instead each spot corresponds to a single, out-of-focus light source.
* "Love bubbles": In anime, manga and associated illustrations, to give a scene a "lovey-dovey" or "dreamy" feeling, often the artist draws many translucent circles in the background and around the edges of the image. While sometimes appearing similar to lens flare, they have no corresponding light source. These can even appear in dark pictures with no bright light sources at all.

wiki.body_clean:
A completely colorless, black-and-white image. The image is composed exclusively of shades of black, white, and grey. It is very common for comics and doujinshi to be in greyscale.

The image may have small highlights of color (known as spot colors), but the image as a whole should be predominately greyscale.

Don't use color tags like black eyes or black hair when tagging greyscale images. The exception is color background tags, so tagging white background, grey background, or black background is fine.

Guidelines
- For completely colorless art, use greyscale.
- For a post consisting of a single color that isn't grey, use monochrome, not greyscale.
- For a mostly greyscale post with a small amount of color as a highlight, use greyscale and spot color.
- For a post using a mix of color and greyscale, use partially colored, not greyscale.
- For a colorless foreground and colorful background, use greyscale with colored background, not greyscale or partially colored.
- For a post that has solid black shadings, use greyscale and high contrast.
- For posts with a small variety of colors but more than two actual colors, use limited palette, not greyscale or monochrome.

wiki.body_clean:
An effect where the edges of an image have a colored, blurry halo or fringe. The RGB color channels appear noticeably offset from one another.

In photography, chromatic aberration is caused by a defect of the camera lens. The lens refracts light of different wavelengths (colors) slightly differently (technically speaking, the index of refraction of a lens material varies depending on the wavelength), causing the colors to become out of focus.

In digital art, chromatic aberration is used to simulate a photographic look or for artistic effect. In small amounts it can increase realism; in greater amounts it can create a sense of motion (similar to motion blur), convey a chaotic environment, or indicate anxiety, paranoia, or mental derangement. In excessive amounts it can induce eyestrain.

Examples

- Wikipedia: Chromatic aberration
- Photography Life: What is Chromatic Aberration?

description.en: Art style, medium, or drawing technique: greyscale.

wiki.body_clean:
A completely colorless, black-and-white image. The image is composed exclusively of shades of black, white, and grey. It is very common for comics and doujinshi to be in greyscale.

The image may have small highlights of color (known as spot colors), but the image as a whole should be predominately greyscale.

Don't use color tags like black eyes or black hair when tagging greyscale images. The exception is color background tags, so tagging white background, grey background, or black background is fine.

Guidelines
- For completely colorless art, use greyscale.
- For a post consisting of a single color that isn't grey, use monochrome, not greyscale.
- For a mostly greyscale post with a small amount of color as a highlight, use greyscale and spot color.
- For a post using a mix of color and greyscale, use partially colored, not greyscale.
- For a colorless foreground and colorful background, use greyscale with colored background, not greyscale or partially colored.
- For a post that has solid black shadings, use greyscale and high contrast.
- For posts with a small variety of colors but more than two actual colors, use limited palette, not greyscale or monochrome.

Examples
- - Spot color

Not greyscale
- Monochrome
- Sepia
- Partially colored
- Limited palette
- Muted colors

Don't use color tags like [[black eyes]] or [[black hair]] when tagging greyscale images. The exception is color background tags, so tagging [[white background]], [[grey background]], or [[black background]] is fine.

h4. Guidelines

* For completely colorless art, use [[greyscale]].
* For a post consisting of a single color that isn't grey, use [[monochrome]], not [[greyscale]].
* For a mostly greyscale post with a small amount of color as a highlight, use [[greyscale]] and [[spot color]].
* For a post using a mix of color and greyscale, use [[partially colored]], not [[greyscale]].
* For a colorless foreground and colorful background, use [[greyscale with colored background]], not [[greyscale]] or [[partially colored]].
* For a post that has solid black shadings, use [[greyscale]] and [[high contrast]].

description.en: Isometric projection

wiki.body_clean:
A method of representing a 3D object on a 2D plane used in technical and engineering drawings. Unlike in perspective drawings or real life, parallel lines do not converge to a vanishing point and objects appear to be the same size regardless of distance.

Note that this tag refers to what is technically called axonometric projection of which isometric projection is a special case. Consequently, many images tagged as isometric on Danbooru may actually be dimetric or trimetric.

wiki.body_clean:
A small icon embedded in text used to express various emotions or concepts.

The word "Emoji" comes from the Japanese word "絵" (e, "picture") + "文字" (moji, "character"). Its resemblance to the word "emoticon" is purely coincidental.

Emoji as we know them originated as a proprietary system by a Japanese mobile phone operator NTT DoCoMo using a Unicode private-use block to encode their emoticons. While other mobile providers used many other systems for emoji, this system was the most compact implementation used at the time (and the closest to the current one).

The very first Emoji were actually Unicode Dingbats, of which, quite a few are now official Emoji. Emoji became a standardized system with its implementation in Unicode 6.0 in 2010 but it's only around 2014-2015 that their use exploded and became commonplace to the point that they became a cultural phenomenon with real world merchandise and even a movie about them.

See emoticon for text-based emoticons like :) or ^_^. See kaomoji for Japanese text-based emoticons like (´・ω・`).

Examples

- 😭 crying emoji
- 😈 demon emoji
- 😳 flushed face emoji
- ❤️ heart emoji
- 🖕 middle finger emoji
- 🤓 nerd emoji

- 🙏 praying emoji

- 🤔 thinking emoji

- wheeze emoji: a variant with open eyes

Emoji as we know them originated as a proprietary system by a Japanese mobile phone operator [[NTT DoCoMo]] using a Unicode private-use block to encode their emoticons. While other mobile providers used many other systems for emoji, this system was the most compact implementation used at the time (and the closest to the current one).

wiki.body_clean:
An establishment where people can come in and order a meal of their choice off a menu, then a waiter or waitress sends the order to the kitchen where a chef and his/her team prepare said meal. The server then returns to the table with the dish, and then the customer pays for it after finishing. This is a very popular business because most people do not have the time to make meals on their own, or don't do it as well as the restaurant does.

Restaurants exist for all three different meals through the day - breakfast, lunch and dinner - and for any type of palate, whether it's American, Japanese, Chinese, Mediterranean and so on. There are also late night and 24/7 places for those who work during the night.

description.en: Sauna

wiki.body_clean:
A sauna is a small room or house designed as a place to experience dry or wet heat sessions, or an establishment with one or more of these and auxiliary facilities.

A sauna session can be a social affair in which the participants disrobe and sit or recline in temperatures typically between 70°C (158 °F) and 100°C (212 °F). This induces relaxation and promotes sweating.

Saunas can be divided into two basic styles: conventional saunas that warm the air or infrared saunas that warm objects. Infrared saunas may use various materials in their heating area such as charcoal, active carbon fibers, and other materials.

description.en: Setting, landscape, or interior feature: street.

wiki.body_clean:
A paved road in a city environment, usually designed for both vehicle and pedestrian traffic.

A street is a type of road. The difference between a road and a street is that road is for all types of roads, including highways and dirt roads outside of cities, while a street generally refers to a paved road in a city. A street is usually designed to accommodate both vehicle and pedestrian traffic, with intersections, traffic lights, sidewalks, and crosswalks. A highway is usually designed only for high-speed or long distance vehicle traffic and doesn't have these features.

A street can be unpaved dirt, but is most often paved with a hard, durable surface such as asphalt, concrete, cobblestone or brick.

Examples
- - External links
- Wikipedia: Street

description.en: Narrow alleyway

wiki.body_clean:
A narrow lane found in cities, often for pedestrians only, which usually runs between or behind buildings.

In older cities and towns in Europe, alleys are often what is left of a medieval street network, or a right of way or ancient footpath in an urban setting. In older urban development, alleys were built to allow for deliveries such as coal to the rear of houses. Alleys may be paved, or simply dirt tracks. A blind alley has no outlet at one end and is thus a cul-de-sac.

description.en: Skyscraper

wiki.body_clean:
A large, continuously habitable building with multiple floors. In modern sources, the height of a skyscraper is defined as being at least 100 meters or 150 meters, but there is no universally accepted definition. Historically, when these types of buildings began to be built in the 1880s, the term first referred to buildings of 10 to 20 stories. Skyscrapers include offices, hotels, residential space, and retail space.

description.en: Planet

wiki.body_clean:
A large spherical astronomical object that typically orbits a star. The tag should be used when at least one planet is seen from outer space or from the surface of another nearby planet. This includes real and fictional planets.

Scientifically, there has always been some ambiguity as to what constitutes a planet, with some celestial bodies such as Pluto and Ceres being considered at different times or by different people either as planets or as "dwarf planets". The International Astronomical Union (IAU) came up with a definition for a planet in 2006, meaning that the planets in our solar system are officially Mercury (planet), Venus, Earth, Mars (planet), Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and neptune, but the definition remains contentious.

Scientifically, there has always been some ambiguity as to what constitutes a planet, with some celestial bodies such as [[Pluto (planet)|]] and Ceres being considered at different times or by different people either as planets or as "dwarf planets". The International Astronomical Union (IAU) came up with a definition for a planet in 2006, meaning that the planets in our solar system are officially [[Mercury_(planet)|]], [[Venus (planet)|]], [[Earth (planet)|]], [[Mars_(planet)|]], [[Jupiter (planet)|]], [[Saturn (planet)|]], [[Uranus (planet)|]] and [[neptune (planet)|]], but the definition remains contentious.

description.en: Weather, season, or natural element: sunflower.

wiki.body_clean:
A native flowering plant from the Americas, recognizable by their single large yellow flower, with an initially greenish center that turns yellow-brown and then blackish as it matures. They typically grow to heights of around 3 meters (10 feet).

Sunflowers come in a variety of colors beyond the common yellow, with colors such as cream color, gold, orange, red, mahogany, and chocolate brown. While the common types only feature a singular flower at the tip of the stem, there are also varieties that grow many additional branching flowers.

Sunflowers are heliotropic while they're developing, meaning they turn to follow the direction of the sun during the day. As they get close to maturing, they stiffen and lose the ability to track the sun. Due to this, most plants mature locked facing towards the east, the direction of the rising sun.

Examples

- Wikipedia: Common Sunflower

description.en: Weather, season, or natural element: rose.

wiki.body_clean:
A type of flower associated with romance, and it is a traditional gift given to a loved one. Each color a rose can be in has specific symbolism as well.

Red Roses: Red roses are the traditional symbol for love and romance. The red rose has long symbolized beauty and perfection. A bouquet of red roses is the perfect way to express your deep feelings for someone special.

Pink Roses: As a symbol of grace and elegance, the pink rose is often given as an expression of admiration. Pink roses can also convey appreciation as well as joyfulness. Pink rose bouquets often impart a gentler meaning than their red counterparts.

Yellow Roses: Yellow roses evokes a feeling of warmth and happiness. The warm feelings associated with the yellow rose are often akin to those shared with a true friend.

Orange Roses: Orange roses are the embodiment of desire and enthusiasm. Orange roses often symbolize passion and excitement and are an expression of fervent romance.

White Roses: Represents purity and innocence. Can also symbolize honor and reverence. Arrangements of White Roses are used to express remembrance.

Purple Roses: With their fantastical appearance, lavender roses are a perfect symbol of enchantment. The lavender rose is also traditionally used to express feelings of love at first sight.

Black Rose: Black roses do not naturally occur in nature. In fiction, they can represent a tragic romance and symbolizes death, hatred, and farewell. If one is about to embark on a long journey that are unlikely to return from, they might be given a black rose as a farewell.

Other roses not seen in nature but are tagged on Danbooru include Blue Roses, Brown Roses, Golden Roses, Green Roses, Grey Roses, and Multicolored Roses.

Note that the Pixiv tag "バラ" (read "bara"), which is literally translated as "rose", is more often used to tag any yaoi or bara content, and as such only apply this tag with the actual flower is seen.

Examples
- External links
- Wikipedia: Rose
- Wikipedia: Rosaceae
