wiki.body_clean:
A genus of flowering plants of the Hydrangeaceae family, native to southern and eastern Asia. Most species are shrubs, but some are small trees. Commonly called hortensia.

Hydrangeas bear globular or umbrella-shaped clusters of flowers that come out any time from early spring to late autumn in a variety of colors influenced by the pH level of the soil. Commonly depicted in shades of blue, purple, and pink.

In Japan, it is commonly associated with the rainy season. Its Japanese name is "ajisai" (アジサイ or 紫陽花), which refers specifically to Hydrangea macrophylla, the bigleaf hydrangea.

In Japan, it is commonly associated with the [[rain]]y season. Its Japanese name is "ajisai" (アジサイ or 紫陽花), which refers specifically to [i]Hydrangea macrophylla[/i], the bigleaf hydrangea.

description.en: Weather, season, or natural element: bamboo.

wiki.body_clean:
A tropical plant consisting of tall, green, tubular stems. It is technically a type of grass, but its woody tissue is as strong as timber, and the tallest species can grow to a height of nearly 100 feet (30 meters). Most species are native to Southeast Asia (around 64%), but the plant is also common in Latin America (around 33%). The rest are native mostly to Africa and Oceania, but North America does have three native species.

Bamboo is used for various purposes, including cooking, construction, textiles, paper, furniture, and traditional medicine.

It is a dietary staple of the giant panda, with which it is frequently depicted.

External links
- Wikipedia: Bamboo

description.en: Object, prop, furniture, or food item: couch.

wiki.body_clean:
A large upholstered piece of furniture designed to seat several people. Also known as a "sofa."

The smallest type of couch, one that seats two people, is referred to as a "loveseat."  A couch with a 90 degree bend in it is a "sectional couch," and as the name suggests is composed of several separate sections.

There may be some overlap between a small "loveseat" type couch and a large easy chair. When in doubt, just tag them as a couch.

Chaise longues (French for "long chair") are also called couches, commonly used as the stereotypical "psychiatrist's couch."

There may be some overlap between a small "loveseat" type couch and a large [[easy chair]]. When in doubt, just tag them as a couch.

[[chaise_longue|Chaise longues]] (French for "long chair") are also called couches, commonly used as the stereotypical "psychiatrist's couch."

description.en: Object, prop, furniture, or food item: chandelier.

wiki.body_clean:
An ornate lighting fixture that hangs from a ceiling.

Early chandeliers used multiple candles for light, but in modern times these have been replaced with electric lamps. Some chandeliers have arrays of crystal prisms to scatter light throughout a room. Due to their size and the amount of light they produce, chandeliers are usually installed as focal points in large rooms such as dining rooms, lounges, or staircases.

Not to be confused with hanging lights, which are of simple design and only have one or two lamps each, and are often used in kitchens and restaurants.
wiki.body_raw:
An ornate lighting fixture that hangs from a [[ceiling]].

Early chandeliers used multiple [[candle|candles]] for light, but in modern times these have been replaced with [[light_bulb|electric lamps]]. Some chandeliers have arrays of crystal prisms to scatter light throughout a room. Due to their size and the amount of light they produce, chandeliers are usually installed as focal points in large rooms such as [[dining_room|dining rooms]], lounges, or [[stairs|staircases]].

Not to be confused with [[hanging light]]s, which are of simple design and only have one or two lamps each, and are often used in [[kitchen]]s and [[restaurant]]s.

description.en: Object, prop, furniture, or food item: candle.

wiki.body_clean:
An object made of wax with a string running from top to bottom which is set alight. Its most common shape is cylindrical.

Has seen more use in the past, but it is still used as a light source in some places, in religious ceremonies and as a symbol of different things such as hope.

If the candles are worn strapped to the head with a headband, there might be a reference to the youkai Hashihime, or the curse ritual Ushi no Koku Mairi (which also involves a mallet or hammer, a straw doll and nails).

description.en: Video game controller
description.zh: game controller（物品、道具、家具与食物）

wiki.body_clean:
A device used to provide input to a computer or video game. Normally this refers to a controller that is separate from the main machine, connected by wire or wirelessly, as opposed to the controls built into a handheld game console such as a Game Boy or Nintendo DS.

Examples of game controllers include gamepads, joysticks, arcade sticks, steering wheel, light guns, the Microsoft Kinect, and many more.

Gamepads can be held conveniently in two hands and do not require any particular mounting surface nor an exact fixed posture from the user. The gamepad provides basic functions to control a game such as Start/Pause, Select, 4- or 8-way navigation, and various different actions via other buttons (numbering from two to roughly a dozen). Among the first gamepads were those game controllers bundled with the U.S.-market Nintendo Entertainment System or Japanese-market Famicom, and throughout the 8-, 16- and 32-bit eras, video game consoles featured gamepads as basic controllers. Since the 64-bit era, they also include analog thumbsticks.

description.en: Object, prop, furniture, or food item: teacup.

wiki.body_clean:
A cup traditionally used to hold tea and other hot beverages. They're typically short and made of ceramic, with a rounded base and a handle. They're often depicted alongside saucers, teapots, and tea sets.

In Japan, tea-drinking may be done with yunomi: these are cylindrical cups without handles. And a chawan is a bowl-shaped cup without handles, found in East Asia.

In China, a traditional cup used for tea-drinking - often seen with a lid - is a gaiwan.

description.en: Object, prop, furniture, or food item: violin.

wiki.body_clean:
A musical instrument of the string family. Basically it consists of a formed, resonating box over which are suspended a fingerboard and four tightened strings. The player holds the larger end under the chin and the opposite end in the hand. Meanwhile, the other hand draws a bow over the strings to make them vibrate; alternately, this strings can be plucked. Said vibrations are amplified in the resonator.

The violin produces notes in the treble range. It may be played with the performer sitting (usually in a chamber or orchestra setting) or standing (often in a solo context). In folk or country music settings, the instrument is often labeled "fiddle."

Examples
- Source: Wikimedia

External links
- Wikipedia: Violin

description.en: Object, prop, furniture, or food item: katana.

wiki.body_clean:
A type of Japanese sword, often called a "samurai sword" because of its historical associations with feudal-era Japan.

It is characterized by its curved, slender, single-edged blade, circular or squared handguard (called the tsuba), and long grip to accommodate two hands (the hilt is often given a distinctive wrapping of silk known as tsuka-ito).

The sword preceding the katana is called a tachi. The general difference between a tachi and a katana is how they are carried. The tachi is suspended from one's waist belt with the cutting edge facing down, while the katana is thrust through the waist belt, edge facing up. Also, in general the tachi is more curved and longer than the katana.

Examples

description.en: Object, prop, furniture, or food item: wand.

wiki.body_clean:
A short, thin, hand-held stick made of wood, stone, ivory, or metal, with ceremonial or magical significance.

It is generally used as a magical tool to cast or channel magic just like a mage staff. Differences between a stave and a wand include a staff being larger (several feet long, about the length of a walking stick and held one- or two-handed) than a wand (usually shorter than two feet, held in one hand or a few fingers) and that a wand is often used in less "serious" works especially by fairies or fairy godmothers and can imply a playful form of magic.

Laevatein, associated with Flandre Scarlet, is an example of a more unusual wand.

Not to be confused with conductor baton, sometimes also referred to as a wand.

description.en: Object, prop, furniture, or food item: ramen.

wiki.body_clean:
A type of Japanese wheat-flour noodle popular in East Asian cuisine, derived from Chinese 'lamian' noodles.

The noodle soup dish of the same name is made by serving ramen noodles in beef or fish broth that is flavored with soy sauce or miso, and topped with a variety of items such as char siu, seaweed, heimuer, narutomaki, softboiled egg, chopped spring onion and kamaboko. There are different flavor distinctions for ramen, such as shio (salty), tonkotsu (pork bone), shoyuu (soy), hiyashi (chilled) and miso.

A food item consisting of two pieces of bread with one or more fillings between them. Different from a burger because sandwiches don't have a beef patty between them, instead using cold cut meats or warmed slices of meat.

description.en: Object, prop, furniture, or food item: donut.

wiki.body_clean:
A donut (also spelled "doughnut") is a small, fried pastry typically glazed with sugar, chocolate, or other frostings. It often contains sweet fillings such as cream, jelly, or custard.

The most common form is the ring-shaped donut, but the term also applies to round, filled donuts and other regional variants. Donuts are popular worldwide and appear frequently in food-related media and illustrations.

In American media, donuts are stereotypically associated with the police, a trope that originated during the interwar period in the United States. Donuts were often the only food readily available during late-night or early morning shifts. To this day, donuts and coffee remain a classic breakfast combination in North American donut shops.

description.en: Object, prop, furniture, or food item: coffee.

wiki.body_clean:
A hot drink that is made by filtering hot water through ground coffee beans, popular for its aroma and concentrated dose of caffeine. Use this tag when coffee itself (ordinarily a black or dark brown liquid) is visible in an image.

It is normally served in a porcelain coffee mug, but it can be taken on the go in a stainless steel mug, styrofoam cup, or in a paper disposable coffee cup. For the traditional porcelain or ceramic "coffee cups" that aren't mug-shaped, see teacup.

As coffee can be quite bitter, it is often served accompanied by sugar and milk or cream. It is usually consumed while hot, but it may be served over ice.

Character is seated.

wiki.body_clean:
The butt resting on a surface (often a chair, couch, or bench), possibly in addition to the legs or feet. For a position with the knees on the floor, use kneeling (except with seiza below).

Examples
- (left to right: yokozuwari, butterfly sitting, wariza, hugging own legs)
- (left to right: indian style, seiza, knees up, wariza, hidden, crossed ankles)

Related tags
Positions
- Butterfly sitting: Rump on floor, knees splayed, soles of feet joined together.
- Crossed legs: Rump on chair, one leg on top of the other at the knee.
- Figure four sitting: in a chair, the ankle or calf of one leg resting on the knee of the other.
- Indian style: Rump on floor, legs crossed at the ankles like a pretzel.
- Lotus position: like Indian style, but with feet placed on opposite thighs with soles facing upward and heels close to the abdomen.
- Seiza: Rump on legs, both legs below body.
- Sitting backwards: in a chair, facing the backrest.
- Sitting sideways: in a chair, facing the side.
- Wariza: Rump on floor, legs bent back on either side.
- Yokozuwari: Rump on floor, legs both to the same side.

Fantasy, science-fiction, or unusual trait: cyberpunk.

wiki.body_clean:
A science fiction genre. Basic themes include the dehumanizing effects of technology, and the accompanying societal breakdown. Think dark and dirty, with lots of wires and neon.

Cyberpunk is a postmodern dystopian genre noted for its focus on ”high tech and low life". The name is a portmanteau of cybernetics and punk, and was originally coined by American science fiction author Bruce Bethke as the title of his short Sci-Fi story Cyberpunk, written in 1980 (and further popularized by the famous American sci-fi author William Gibson).

Cyberpunk can cover numerous themes and motifs but generally involve reflecting on the current anxieties of society and amping them up to an extreme; things like mass surveillance, corporate monopolization, climate change, mass media, artificial intelligence and any other themes can thus be accommodated by a cyberpunk setting.

For the series of the same name, see Cyberpunk.

description.en: Fantasy, science-fiction, or unusual trait: demon horns.

wiki.body_clean:
The horns of a demon girl, or demon boy.

They come in two broad varieties:
- short and stubby with an upward/inward curve, as in the emoticon: 😈 Common in simple illustrations and comedy. Similar to cow horns.
- long with elaborate curvature. Common in complex illustrations. Frequently resemble sheep or goat horns, including a bumpy, textured surface. Alternately, they may appear smooth and metallic.

In both versions, the horns are usually attached to the sides or top of the head. This is in contrast to skin-covered horns, which are usually attached to the forehead.

Examples
- Short
- Long

description.en: Fantasy, science-fiction, or unusual trait: antlers.

wiki.body_clean:
A pair of branched solid bone horn-like structures that arise from the frontal bone on the head of animals of the deer family. Unlike horns, antlers are branched, quickly develop underneath a covering of furry skin called velvet, consist of dead bone once fully developed, and regularly shed over the course of the animal's life (most commonly every year).

Not to be confused with Eastern dragon horns, which also branch, but are thicker and are categorized as horns.

Examples
- deer antlers
- reindeer antlers
- moose antlers

description.en: Fantasy, science-fiction, or unusual trait: elf.

wiki.body_clean:
A humanoid fantasy race characterized by their grace, finesse, and youthful appearance despite long lifespans. Popularized in their modern form by Tolkien's Legendarium.

Their most common traits are long blonde hair and pointy ears.

They are commonly portrayed as forest-dwellers living in tune with nature, often wearing green and brown clothing. They tend to use bows as their weapon of choice and are sometimes powerful magic users.

description.en: Fantasy, science-fiction, or unusual trait: vampire.

wiki.body_clean:
A being in folklore who feeds on the blood of living creatures. Notable characteristics include fangs, predatory eyes, pale skin and a bite mark on the neck.

Although typically described as undead, a vampire could be a living person. Popularized in Europe in the 18th century and codified in literature in the 19th century as a Western folkloric being distinct from its Slavic(-Turkic) roots.

Common beliefs about vampires include that they are immortal, that they can only be killed by being exposed to the sun or by a wooden stake driven through their heart, that they sleep in coffins, have no reflections, are afraid of crosses and garlic, are able to hypnotize victims, are able to transform into bats, and that they are unable to enter homes without being invited in. Half-vampires are often called 'dhampir' in English, which means vampire in Albanian.

This tag should not be used unless vampiric traits are clearly visible in the image. See vampire costume for when a character is simply dressed as a vampire.

For the game produced by Capcom, see Darkstalkers.

Examples
- Notable vampire characters
- Dracula from Bram Stoker's Dracula
- Akashiya Moka from Rosario+Vampire
- Alucard, Carmilla and Dracula from Castlevania
- Alucard from Hellsing
- Arcueid Brunestud from Tsukihime 
- Demitri Maximoff from Darkstalkers
- Dio Brando from JoJo no Kimyou na Bouken
- Flandre Scarlet and Remilia Scarlet from Touhou
- Kuzuha from Nijisanji
- Marceline Abadeer from Adventure Time
- Rachel Alucard from Blazblue
- Slayer and Nagoriyuki from Guilty Gear
- Vampy from Granblue Fantasy
- Yozora Mel from Hololive
- Morbius from Marvel Comics 
- Count von Count from Sesame Street

description.ru: Ламия, мифическое существо с чертами змеи
description.en: Lamia, mythical serpent-like creature

wiki.body_clean:
A lamia (alternatively, a naga) is a monster girl whose upper body is human and whose lower body is snake-like. Despite having different cultural origins, the two are rendered so similarly as to make it merely a matter of style which one a serpent-legged character will be called.

The term naga comes from Hinduism and Buddhism, and literally means "cobra". Naga can appear with varying degrees of humanity, but typically have fully human torsos. The term lamia comes from Greek, though its original usage did not possess snake-like qualities. It was only in the 1600s that Robert Burton ascribed the familiar qualities, which were subsequently popularized by John Keats in his poem lamia published in July 1820.

The Japanese, apparently not having either of these myths as a major part of their tradition, tend to ascribe lamia/naga with personalities like those they associate with snakes in general and lamia are often the tsundere types.

Notable Lamias
- Alipheese Fateburn XVI from Mon-Musu Quest!
- Cassiopeia from League of Legends
- Deis from Breath of Fire
- Echidna from Granblue Fantasy
- Echidna from Puzzle & Dragons
- Jashin-chan from Jashin-chan Dropkick
- Kiyohime from Fate/Grand Order
- Lamia Hygieia from Mamonomusume to no Seikatsu
- Miia from Monster Musume no Iru Nichijou
- Saphentite Neikes from Monster Musume no Oisha-san

description.en: Fantasy, science-fiction, or unusual trait: android.

wiki.body_clean:
A robot that looks human, or very nearly human, with a fully human face.

They may appear male, female, or androgynous. Female androids, also known as gynoids, are the most common in anime. Androids often have small robotic appendages or markings to make it apparent they are not human. The most common of these are robot ears, robot joints, skin seams, mechanical wings, and attached cables.

The difference between a humanoid robot and an android is that an android looks mostly human, usually having something resembling skin (though it needn't be skin-colored) and a fully human face, while a humanoid robot is clearly non-human, with a non-human face.

This tag should not be used if the character looks completely human, with no visible robotic traits. Tag what you see, not what you know.

Not to be confused with cyborg, which is a person augmented with mechanical body parts.

Examples
- Aigis
- Dorothy Haze
- A2
- Yurizaki Mira
- KOS-MOS (Ver. 4)

External links
- Wikipedia: Android

description.en: Fantasy, science-fiction, or unusual trait: cyborg.

wiki.body_clean:
An organism that is made up of both cybernetic and organic components. In anime, this generally refers to humans that have been altered to be partially robotic.

It can be difficult to tell a cyborg apart from an android, especially when dealing with original characters and those whose origins are unknown. In cases like these, one should examine any visible robotic components. If they appear to be added-on or function as prosthetics, that character is likely a cyborg. If you are unable to determine whether the character is a cyborg or purely robotic, it's best to tag them as android until more information can be found.

description.en: Fantasy, science-fiction, or unusual trait: mecha.

wiki.body_clean:
Mecha (メカ - me-ka) are giant robots, robot vehicles, robot construction equipment, robot mobile buildings and generally over-sized robot machines. While the original Japanese definition extends to include power armor, exoskeletons, and general sci-fi machinery, for danbooru purposes this tag is for piloted and/or giant robots.

Primarily seen in science fiction settings, though there are several cases of them in fantasy settings.

Types of Mecha
- Externally piloted mecha - A mecha where the controls are external and the pilot rides on top of the machine.

description.en: Fantasy, science-fiction, or unusual trait: power armor.

wiki.body_clean:
Power Armor is a term commonly used to describe full-body armor that not only protects, but enhances physical capabilities. Unlike regular body armor, this includes some form of powered exoskeleton or power suit to act as mechanical muscle, reducing the user's amount of work to do just about anything. A common form of armor in science fiction and tokusatsu, especially in space environments - a popular example is Samus Aran.

One of the first appearances of power armor in science fiction was in the novel Starship Troopers (1959).

description.en: Fantasy, science-fiction, or unusual trait: zombie.

wiki.body_clean:
Reanimated human or animal corpse. Stereotypical zombies are characterized by animalistic behavior, indifference to pain, and an insatiable hunger for human flesh (particularly brains). Some zombies walk with a stiff gait and outstretched arms due to rigor mortis. They are a common monster in horror fiction and video games due to their predatory nature and tendency to shrug off debilitating injury.

Only characters with visible evidence of death or decomposition should be tagged zombie. Unnatural grayish-blue or green skin, blank eyes, and festering wounds are good indicators of when this tag should be used. Whether or not a character is canonically a zombie is irrelevant.

description.en: Adult nudity or anatomical attribute: uncensored.

wiki.body_clean:
An image that has not been censored by the artist. See decensored for images that have been decensored by a third-party.

This tag applies only to genitalia, sex acts, body fluids, or other things that would normally be censored. It does not apply to nipples, or to body parts that aren't fully visible. It can apply if only part of the image is left uncensored.

In Japan, it is illegal to draw uncensored genitalia if they are to be published publicly for domestic distribution. Some artists skirt around this law by applying censorship that is easy to remove, or by applying pointless censorship that barely hides the censored body part. Others maintain a non-Japanese presence to bypass Japanese laws altogether and distribute uncensored versions of their work. It is also noted that some censorship also doubles as a paywall or sample work of sorts, with the uncensored version available in an artists' donation page, such as Patreon, Fanbox and others.

description.en: Animal, creature, or animal-like feature: wolf.

wiki.body_clean:
Commonly known as a gray wolf, a species of canid native to the wilderness and remote areas of North America, Eurasia, and North Africa. It is the largest member of its family, with males averaging 43–45 kg (95–99 lb), and females 36–38.5 kg (79–85 lb) It is similar in general appearance and proportions to a german shepherd, or sled dog, but has a larger head, narrower chest, longer legs, straighter tail and bigger paws. Its winter fur is long and bushy, and is usually mottled gray in color, though it can range from nearly pure white, red, or brown to black.

Touhou character Inubashiri Momiji is a wolf tengu.

description.en: Animal, creature, or animal-like feature: fox.

wiki.body_clean:
A small omnivorous wild canine genus (Vulpes) that consists of numerous species around the world, as well as colloquially including a few similar non-Vulpes canids. Foxes are best known for their bushy tails and pointed snouts, as well as their curious and playful behavior.

Foxes are very important to Japanese folklore, being the center of the kitsune myths, often being depicted with multiple tails - up to a total of nine.

Young foxes are called kits.

description.en: Animal, creature, or animal-like feature: tanuki.

wiki.body_clean:
The Japanese name for the Japanese raccoon dog. In Japanese folklore, a tanuki is a playful shape-shifting traditional youkai.

Not to be confused for the raccoon, which looks similar to the tanuki but is not the same animal. A key difference is their fur color: tanuki tend to have brown fur while raccoons have grey fur.

The words "tanuki" (狸), "mujina" (貉), and "mami" (猯) were historically confused in Japan. "Mujina" and "mami" used to mean badgers in some areas, while on the other areas these terms used to mean raccoon dogs. There are some areas in which badgers were called tanuki.

In folklore, a type of tanuki called the mamedanuki (豆狸) sports comically huge testicles. Shigaraki ware, a type of traditional Japanese pottery, often depicted these tanuki. The statues depicted a mamedanuki as he transforms (or fails to transform) into an errand boy going out to buy sake at a liquor shop.

External links
- Wikipedia: Tanuki
- Wikipedia: Mujina
- Wikipedia: Japanese raccoon dog

wiki.body_clean:
The tiger (Panthera tigris) is a member of the Felidae family and the largest and possibly most dangerous of the five "big cats".
Native to much of eastern and southern Asia, the Tiger is an apex predator and an obligate carnivore. Aside from their great bulk and power, their most recognisable feature is a pattern of dark vertical stripes that overlays near-white to reddish-orange fur, with lighter underparts.

description.en: Animal, creature, or animal-like feature: crow.

wiki.body_clean:
A large, all-black passerine bird.

Scientifically, crows are one species of bird in the broader Corvidae family, which includes crows, ravens, rooks, jackdaws, jays, magpies, treepies, choughs, and nutcrackers. On Danbooru, "crow" includes all visually-similar birds in the Corvidae family.

Birds in the Corvidae family range in size from the relatively small pigeon-size jackdaws (Eurasian and Daurian) to the Common Raven of the Holarctic region and Thick-billed Raven of the highlands of Ethiopia. The 40 or so members of Corvus genus occur on all temperate continents (except South America) and several offshore and oceanic islands.

Crow species found in Japan, aside from magpies, jays and nutcrackers, include the rook, carrion crow, Eurasian & Daurian jackdaws, the large-billed crow, and the common raven.

Touhou characters Shameimaru Aya and Himekaidou Hatate are crow tengu, while Reiuji Utsuho is a hell raven youkai.

External links
- Wikipedia: Corvidae
- Wikipedia: List of birds of Japan

Birds in the Corvidae family range in size from the relatively small pigeon-size jackdaws (Eurasian and Daurian) to the Common Raven of the Holarctic region and Thick-billed Raven of the highlands of Ethiopia. description.en: Animal, creature, or animal-like feature: bee.

wiki.body_clean:
A flying insect that pollinates flowers and produces honey and beeswax. They live as colonies and build beehives to store their honey, and possess stingers that inject minuscule amounts of venom in anyone they deem intruders.

The most common type of bee is the European honey bee. Human management of honey bee colonies for honey production is called apiculture or beekeeping.

description.en: Animal, creature, or animal-like feature: orca.

wiki.body_clean:
The Orca (Orcinus orca) is a black and white carnivorous marine mammal. Commonly known as the killer whale and also known as orca whale. The orca is the largest species of dolphin, being part of the family Delphinidae. (Delphinidae is within the Odontoceti or toothed whales, which is within the Cetacea or whales, so orcas are whales in the sense that all dolphins are whales.)

Despite this, works portraying an Orca ought not be tagged as whale.

Usually growing around 5-8 meters long, orcas are known to be apex predators of the sea, as they have no natural predators.
wiki.body_raw:
The [b]Orca[/b] ([i]Orcinus orca[/i]) is a black and white carnivorous marine mammal. Commonly known as the [b]killer whale[/b] and also known as [b]orca whale[/b]. The orca is the largest species of dolphin, being part of the family Delphinidae. (Delphinidae is within the Odontoceti or toothed whales, which is within the Cetacea or whales, so orcas are whales in the sense that all dolphins are whales.)

Despite this, works portraying an Orca [b]ought not[/b] be tagged as [[whale]].

Usually growing around 5-8 meters long, orcas are known to be apex predators of the sea, as they have no natural predators.

description.en: Animal, creature, or animal-like feature: snout.

wiki.body_clean:
The protruding portion of an animal's face, consisting of its nose, mouth, and jaw. In many animals, the equivalent structure is called a muzzle, rostrum, or proboscis.

Snouts are found on many mammals in a variety of shapes. Some animals, including ursines and great cats, have box-like snouts, while others, like shrews, have pointed snouts. Pig snouts are flat and cylindrical.

Furry characters often show their snouts on a profile view, similarly to how human anime characters only show the contour of their noses on a profile view.

Examples
- - External links
- Wikipedia: Snout

description.en: Animal, creature, or animal-like feature: muzzle.
Animal, creature, or animal-like feature: fangs.

wiki.body_clean:
A character with multiple prominent canine teeth, such as with vampires or various animals.

Distinct from fang, which is a single visible prominent canine tooth. This is a visual trait often meant to emphasize a specific aspect of a character's personality.

Distinct from sharp teeth, where all of a character's teeth are sharp - although it is possible for a character to have both, if the canines are noticeably larger than the rest.

Opposite of tusks which are typically larger lower teeth, usually on orcs or mammoths.

Examples
- - Skin fangs
- Fangs out
